section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the innovation of teshuvah in returning sparks to their source is specifically accomplished through Jewish souls, because the power to make a dwelling place for G-d in the lower worlds is rooted in the Awtsmoos.
section.t: And one may add,
that also the innovation in teshuvah of returning the sparks
(that are in physical things)
to their source,
is specifically through the souls of Israel63
(by performing mitzvos with physical things,
or by using them for the sake of Heaven).
And it can be said that this is in the manner explained elsewhere64
that the power to make a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, in the lower worlds is specifically in the souls of Israel, because since "world" is from the term concealment and hiding65,
behold, that the world becomes a vessel for G-dliness
(the opposite of the nature and definition of world)
is an innovation66,
and in the manner of the innovation of creation ex nihilo, which is in the power of the Awtsmoos67,
and therefore the making of a dwelling place in the lower worlds is specifically through the souls of Israel,
for because the souls are rooted in the Awtsmoos,
therefore this power is given to them.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section reconciles two interpretations of "one hour of teshuvah and good deeds," explaining that teshuvah is superior in essential delight while good deeds have the advantage of innovation and completing the purpose of a dwelling place, with teshuvah serving as a prerequisite for good deeds.
section.t: And based on this, one can reconcile the two interpretations of "one hour of teshuvah and good deeds,"
for according to one interpretation teshuvah is more elevated than good deeds,
and according to one interpretation teshuvah is a prerequisite for good deeds,
for that teshuvah is more elevated than good deeds is that the delight of teshuvah
(of the soul)
is an essential delight as mentioned above,
except that nevertheless there is an advantage in good deeds over teshuvah from the aspect of the innovation in this
(as above),
and also because specifically through this the intention of a dwelling place in the lower worlds is completed68.
And teshuvah is a prerequisite for good deeds,
for since the power to make a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, in the lower worlds is specifically in the souls
(as above),
therefore,
in order that the dwelling place made through the performance of mitzvos be in completeness and revelation,
good deeds that are luminous,
it is through the precedence of teshuvah,
the revelation of the root of the soul, until [the level] where it is rooted in the Awtsmoos.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section parallels the two aspects of teshuvah with the teshuvah of Rosh Hashanah and the teshuvah of the Ten Days of Repentance, explaining that the former is a return to the source while the latter is a preparation for Torah and mitzvos, as seen in the days between Yom Kippur and Sukkos.
section.t: And behold, the two matters mentioned above in teshuvah,
that it is a matter in itself and that it is a prerequisite for good deeds,
are analogous to the teshuvah of Rosh Hashanah and the teshuvah of the Ten Days of Repentance.
For the teshuvah of Rosh Hashanah,
alluded to in the shofar blast69,
its essence is
(not teshuvah over particular matters,
but rather)
the return to its source and root70.
And the matter of the "strait" of the shofar is
(not a strait of "and for sins,"
but rather)
that it is "with" and not the expanse where it is rooted71.
For this is the connection of the shofar with "accept Me as your King,"
for the matter of "accept Me as your King" is the drawing down of kingship from its root and source.
And the teshuvah of the Ten Days of Repentance
[for then is the building of the ten Sefiros of Malchus72,
the particulars of Malchus]
pertains to particulars.
And it is a prerequisite for Torah and mitzvos
(good deeds)
whose beginning is in the four days between Yom Kippur and Sukkos,
as it is stated in the Midrash73
that in these days one is occupied with his sukkah and one with his lulav,
sukkah which is the encompassing [light] of the aspect of mitzvos,
garments74,
and lulav whose matter is the drawing down into internality
[as is known75
that through taking the four species the encompassing [light] of the sukkah is drawn into internality],
the aspect of Torah,
and "Your Torah is within my innards"76.
And particularly in the four species themselves,
and the highest among them is the lulav which has taste, alluding to Torah77.
And these two matters,
which in the four days before Sukkos are in the form of preparation
(occupied with his sukkah and his lulav),
on the festival of Sukkos are actualized78.
